source.title: The Volume of Vector Fields on Riemannian Manifolds: Main Results and Open Problems

accepted.question_text: Let S^{2m+1} be the unit odd-dimensional sphere in R^{2m+2}, let N be its outward unit normal field, and call a vector field of the form r JN a Hopf vector field, where J is a complex structure on R^{2m+2} and r > 0 is constant. Is every smooth minimal vector field of constant length on S^{2m+1} a Hopf vector field?
accepted.context_brief: Hopf-field uniqueness for minimal vector fields

evidence.quote: the vector field of the form J N is known as a Hopf field
Conjecture 3.1 The only minimal smooth vector fields of constant length on the odd-dimensional spheres are the Hopf vector fields.

accepted.question_text: For each integer m > 1 and each r > 0, determine the number V(m,r) defined as the infimum of Vol(V) over all smooth vector fields V of constant length r on the odd-dimensional sphere S^{2m+1}, where Vol(V) is the volume of the submanifold V(S^{2m+1}) in the tangent bundle with the Sasaki metric. If the infimum is attained, characterize all smooth length-r vector fields that attain it.
accepted.context_brief: Main infimum problem on odd spheres

evidence.quote: The main open problem is to compute the infimum of the volume of smooth vector fields of constant length
and to characterise the smooth vector fields minimising the functional

accepted.question_text: For m > 1 and r > 0, radial vector fields on punctured odd-dimensional spheres give a lower bound c(m,r) vol(S^{2m+1}) for the volume of smooth constant-length vector fields on S^{2m+1}, but this lower bound cannot be attained by a smooth vector field. Can c(m,r) vol(S^{2m+1}) nevertheless be approached as a limit of volumes of smooth vector fields of constant length r on S^{2m+1}?
accepted.context_brief: Approachability of the radial lower bound

evidence.quote: it’s not known if this value can be approached by the volume of smooth vector fields.

accepted.question_text: For each m > 1, define r1(m) as a threshold such that for r > r1(m) the Hopf vector fields of length r on S^{2m+1} have less volume than the parallel-transport vector fields used to produce the alternative upper bound c*(m,r) vol(S^{2m+1}). Determine explicit values or a formula for r1(m), and clarify its relation to the instability threshold r0(m) = sqrt(2m - 3).
accepted.context_brief: Threshold comparing Hopf and parallel-transport bounds

evidence.quote: Whether the upper bound of .V (m; r) coming from parallel transport vector fields is better
We don’t know the explicit values of .r1 (m)

accepted.question_text: Consider the variations of Hopf vector fields on S^{2m+1} that start at a Hopf vector field, decrease volume for small positive parameter values, and converge to a parallel-transport vector field. For which m and r are these variations volume-decreasing for the entire parameter interval, not only infinitesimally near the Hopf vector field?

evidence.quote: These variations starting at Hopf vector fields are decreasing volume for small t
we don’t know if they are volume decreasing for all t.

accepted.question_text: Let M be a complete (2m+1)-dimensional Riemannian manifold of constant positive curvature that is not the sphere, and consider smooth vector fields on M of fixed constant length r > 0. Is the infimum of the volume functional over such vector fields attained exactly by Hopf vector fields?
accepted.context_brief: Hopf minimizers on positive-curvature space forms

evidence.quote: Conjecture 5.1 On a complete .(2m + 1)-dimensional manifold M of constant curvature
the infimum of the volume of vector fields of constant length is attained exactly by Hopf vector fields.

accepted.question_text: Let (S^{2m+1}, g_mu) be a Berger sphere with m > 1, let H_mu be its unit Hopf vector field, and let rH_mu be the Hopf vector field scaled to length r. Complete the classification, in the parameters m, mu, and r, of when rH_mu is stable as an r-minimal vector field for the volume functional.
accepted.context_brief: Stability of scaled Hopf fields on Berger spheres

evidence.quote: For .m > 1 the situation becomes quite complicated and the problem is not completely solved.
Open Problem To complete the classification of .rHμ attending its stability as an r-minimal vector field

accepted.question_text: Let a finite subgroup G of U(m+1) act freely by isometries on the Berger sphere (S^{2m+1}, g_mu), and let H_mu^G be the induced unit Hopf vector field on the quotient S^{2m+1}/G. Determine the values of mu, depending on G and m, for which H_mu^G is stable, including the open case of projective spaces with m odd.

evidence.quote: The stability problem is still open in general
find the values of .μG for which .HμG is stable

accepted.question_text: For the three-dimensional Berger sphere (S^3, g_mu) with mu > 1 and for a prescribed constant length r > 0, determine the infimum of the volume functional among all vector fields of length r. In particular, identify whether the infimum is attained and, if so, characterize the minimizers.
accepted.context_brief: Volume minimizers on Berger 3-spheres with mu greater than one

evidence.quote: find the infimum of the volume of vector fields of constant length for the 3-dimensional spheres with .μ > 1.
this lower bound is never attained

accepted.question_text: On the two-sphere S^2, consider vector fields V of constant length r != 1 that are defined without boundary, and let Sigma_V be the associated surface in the sphere tangent bundle. The known area-minimization theorem assumes that Sigma_V is homeomorphic to a projective plane. Can this projective-plane topology assumption be removed while still concluding that the parallel-transport vector fields are the only area minimizers?
accepted.context_brief: Removing topology assumptions for S2 area minimizers

evidence.quote: parallel transport vector fields are the only minimisers of the area
whether the additional assumption of .ΣV to be homeomorphic to a projective plane can be avoided.

accepted.question_text: For even-dimensional spheres S^{2m} with m > 1, restrict attention to unit vector fields defined on the sphere minus one point. Is the analogue of the S^2 theorem true: are the least-area unit vector fields exactly the parallel-transport vector fields?
accepted.context_brief: Even-dimensional sphere analogue of the S2 theorem

evidence.quote: Among vector fields of constant length defined on .S 2 minus one point
whether a similar result is also true for other even dimensional spheres

accepted.question_text: For Lie groups and homogeneous spaces with known examples of minimal unit vector fields, determine the second variation of the volume functional at those fields and classify which examples are stable. In particular, go beyond the known computations for invariant minimal unit vector fields on three-dimensional Lie groups.
accepted.context_brief: Second variation and stability on Lie groups

evidence.quote: the only results concerning the second variation of the volume of vector fields on Lie groups
It would be interesting to have a deeper knowledge of the stability

accepted.question_text: For the three-dimensional Berger sphere with mu > 1, the Hopf unit vector field is not energy-minimizing because there are unit vector fields in the two-dimensional span generated by the orthogonal fields E1 and E2 with smaller energy. Which unit vector fields actually minimize the energy functional in this case?

evidence.quote: for all unit vector fields X in the 2-dimensional space generated by .{E1 , E2 }
we don’t know if these vector fields are the minimisers.

trace.notes: Normalized the single input URL as a zbMATH resolver record with trailing identifier 7733664.

Local resolver metadata in outputs/open-problems-0418-all.csv and outputs/shards/open-problems-shard-1.csv identified the exact work title and DOI 10.1007/978-3-031-36857-8. The direct zbMATH page and zbMATH API were unavailable to local shell fetching because DNS resolution is blocked in the sandbox. The Springer landing page confirmed the same title, author, DOI, and table of contents but exposed only preview text. Exact-title recovery found a readable full-text HTML copy whose title, author, ISBNs, DOI, and contents match the same work; this HTML page was used as the primary extraction artifact.

Mapped the HTML source into front matter, Chapter 1 Introduction, Chapter 2 Minimal Sections of Tensor Bundles, Chapter 3 Minimal Vector Fields of Constant Length on the Odd-Dimensional Spheres, Chapter 4 Vector Fields of Constant Length of Minimum Volume on the Odd-Dimensional Spherical Space Forms, Chapter 5 Vector Fields of Constant Length on Punctured Spheres, and References. Open-problem regions were concentrated in the introduction, Chapter 3 notes, Chapter 4 Berger-sphere discussion, and Chapter 5 Sections 5.3-5.4.

Extracted the Gluck-Ziller minimum-volume problem, the question of whether Hopf fields are the only smooth minimal vector fields, the Berger-sphere mu greater than one minimizer problem, and the central odd-sphere infimum problem from the introduction.

Extracted Conjecture 3.1, the stability classification problem for scaled Hopf fields on Berger spheres, the quotient Berger-sphere stability threshold problem, the vague stability-geometry relation question, the rough-Laplacian proof-method suggestion, and the second-variation problem for Lie-group examples.
Extracted the 3-dimensional Berger-sphere volume-infimum question for mu greater than one and the related energy-minimizer question.

Extracted the main odd-sphere volume-infimum problem, approachability of the radial lower bound, explicit r1(m) threshold problem, monotonicity of Hopf-to-parallel-transport variations, Conjecture 5.1 for positive-curvature quotients, the S2 projective-plane-topology question, and the even-dimensional sphere analogue question.

Rewrote accepted candidates as standalone questions, inlining the definitions of Hopf field, Berger sphere notation, constant-length vector field, volume functional, quotient notation, Sigma_V, and relevant minimization classes when supported by the source text.

Moved two candidates to needs_review: one because the source question asks whether a geometric fact is related to stability without specifying a precise mathematical target, and one because it asks for a proof of referenced propositions whose full statements would need more context than the local quote provides.
Merged the S3-only formulation and the all odd-dimensional-spheres formulation into the broader Conjecture 3.1 item.

Kept the main infimum problem, lower-bound approachability, threshold computation, variation monotonicity, quotient minimizer conjecture, Berger-sphere stability, Berger-sphere volume minimization, S2 topology assumption, even-sphere analogue, Lie-group stability, and energy-minimizer question separate because they ask for different objects or occur in different geometric settings.

Accepted items passed the self-containedness, evidence coverage, evidence completeness, no-new-facts, source adequacy, solved-status metadata, and schema conformance gates. No accepted item is marked solved because the primary source does not label any of these problems as solved or resolve them.
Needs-review items failed the precision or cross-reference gates and were not accepted.
Saved final JSON to outputs/parse-paper/7733664.json and outputs/latest.json.
